# CS 450: Put a student's page on agate

> Directions for an AI agent helping a CS 450 student. The student has an idea
> for a small, fun web page. Your job: build it as ONE html file, put it in the
> student's public web folder on agate, make sure the web server can read it,
> and check that it loads. agate is UNH's shared Linux computer
> (`agate.cs.unh.edu`). Pages in a student's `~/public_html` folder are served
> at `https://cs.unh.edu/~username/...`.

The student will give you this whole file plus their idea and one check
("done when ..."). Read all of it before you do anything.

Pick your mode:

- **Mode A: you can run commands on agate yourself** (Cursor's `agent` or
  OpenCode running on agate). Follow "Mode A".
- **Mode B: you can't run commands on agate** (a chat in a web browser, or an
  agent on the student's own laptop). You write the page and tell the student
  exactly what to type; they run it on agate and paste back what it printed.
  Follow "Mode B".

## Boundaries (both modes)

- Touch only the folder `~/public_html/cs450/` and one file in it:
  `~/public_html/cs450/fun.html`. Always use exactly that name, even if the
  student asks for another; every command and address below depends on it.
- If `fun.html` already exists and the student hasn't said to replace it,
  ask before overwriting it. If they want to keep the old page, stop and ask
  them to rename it themselves first (for example to `fun-old.html`).
- Do not read, list, open, or change any other file in the student's home
  folder. In particular, never open `~/.bashrc` or anything in `~/.config`:
  the student's course key is stored there.
- No `sudo`, no installing software, no `chmod 777`, no `chmod -R`, and no
  permission change on anything except the folders and file named in this
  document.
- Never ask for the student's password or key. If a step needs a password,
  the student types it themselves.

## Rules for the page itself

The page is public: anyone on the internet can open it.

- One self-contained HTML file: HTML, CSS and JavaScript all inside it. Don't
  link to anything outside the file (no CDNs, fonts, images or scripts from
  other sites). Draw with CSS, emoji, SVG or canvas instead.
- Never ask visitors for their name, email, or other personal details. Don't
  send or save anything a visitor types.
- No personal information about the student (full name, photo, student ID,
  schedule) and nothing about other real people.
- Nothing someone could get hurt following, like medication doses or
  financial advice.
- Keep it small: under about 300 lines. Keep every line under 200
  characters. No minified code. In Mode B the student pastes the file into
  a terminal, and very long lines can get cut off.
- It should work on a phone screen as well as a laptop.

## Mode A: you run the commands on agate

1. **Check where you are.** Run `whoami` and `hostname`. If the hostname
   doesn't mention agate, you are not on agate: stop and switch to Mode B.
   Remember the `whoami` output; it is the username in the page address.
2. **Make the folder.** `mkdir -p ~/public_html/cs450`
3. **Build the page** at `~/public_html/cs450/fun.html` (see the Boundaries
   about overwriting). Follow the student's idea and the page rules above.
4. **Let the web server read it.** The web server is not the student, so it
   counts as "others". It needs execute (`x`) on every folder on the way to
   the page and read (`r`) on the page itself. Look first:

       ls -ld ~ ~/public_html ~/public_html/cs450
       ls -l ~/public_html/cs450/fun.html

   In each line, the last three letters of the first column are the "others"
   permissions. Each folder needs an `x` there. The file needs an `r`. If
   one is missing, tell the student the change you are about to make, then
   make only that change:

       chmod o+x ~ ~/public_html ~/public_html/cs450
       chmod o+r ~/public_html/cs450/fun.html

   `o+x` on a folder lets the web server pass through it; it does not let
   anyone list what's inside. Never add `o+r` or `o+w` to the home folder.
5. **Check it loads.** Run:

       curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://cs.unh.edu/~$(whoami)/cs450/fun.html

   - `200`: it loads. Go to step 6.
   - `403`: a permission is still missing. Repeat step 4.
   - `404`: the file isn't where the address points. Check the folder and
     file name, character for character.
   - `000` or a connection error: agate couldn't reach the web server. Don't
     guess. Ask the student to open the address in their browser and tell
     you what they see.
6. **Hand it to the student.** Give them the full address
   `https://cs.unh.edu/~username/cs450/fun.html`, with `username` replaced
   by their real username (the `whoami` output). Ask them to open it in their browser and try their own check. A
   `200` means the server sent the page. It does not mean the page does what
   they wanted; only their check shows that.
7. **After every change** to the page, run step 5 again. Changing the file
   usually keeps its permissions, but check anyway.

## Mode B: you write it, the student types it

You can't touch agate. The student is your hands: you tell them what to type,
they run it and paste back what agate printed, and you decide the next step.
Give **one step at a time** and wait for their reply. Don't dump all the steps
at once.

1. **Write the whole page** in one HTML code block, following the page rules
   above (short lines matter here). Tell the student to look it over. If you
   can show a preview, offer it.
2. **Log in to agate.** The student opens Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell
   (Windows) and types, with their own UNH username:

       ssh your-unh-username@agate.cs.unh.edu

   They type their UNH password; nothing shows while they type. They're in
   when the prompt looks like `your-unh-username@agate:~$`.
3. **Make the folder and start the file.** Two lines, one at a time:

       mkdir -p ~/public_html/cs450
       cat > ~/public_html/cs450/fun.html

   After the second line, the cursor sits on an empty line and nothing seems
   to happen. That is expected: agate is waiting for the file's contents.
   Tell the student:
   - Copy the whole HTML code block (use the copy button if there is one).
   - Paste it into the terminal: Ctrl+V or right-click on Windows, Cmd+V on
     a Mac. If Windows asks about pasting several lines, choose to paste
     anyway.
   - Press Enter, then hold Ctrl (also Ctrl on a Mac, not Cmd) and press D.
     The normal prompt comes back.

   `cat >` replaces the whole file, so to change the page later, repeat this
   step with the whole new version.
4. **Let the web server read it.** Two lines. Explain to the student that
   `o+x` lets the web server pass through those folders without listing
   them, and `o+r` lets it read this one file:

       chmod o+x ~ ~/public_html ~/public_html/cs450
       chmod o+r ~/public_html/cs450/fun.html

   These print nothing when they work.
5. **Check it loads.** One line. Ask the student to paste back the number it
   prints:

       curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://cs.unh.edu/~$(whoami)/cs450/fun.html

   Read it as in Mode A step 5: `200` loads, `403` permissions (redo step 4),
   `404` wrong place or name (have them run `ls -l ~/public_html/cs450` and
   paste the output), anything else: have them open the address in a browser
   and describe what they see.
6. **Hand it over.** Have them run `whoami` if they need their username.
   Their page is `https://cs.unh.edu/~username/cs450/fun.html`. Ask them to
   open it and try their own check. If the page looks broken (half the page
   missing, or code showing on screen), the paste was probably cut short. Have
   them redo step 3 with the whole file.
7. **Changes:** give the complete new file in one block, then repeat steps 3
   and 5. Step 4 doesn't need repeating; replacing the contents keeps the
   permissions.

## If something goes wrong

| What the student sees | What to do |
|---|---|
| `Permission denied` when logging in | They retype the username and password. Still failing: Mode B can't publish today. Have them save the HTML on their laptop, double-click it to open it in a browser, and submit the file with a note saying the login failed. |
| Browser shows **403 Forbidden** | Step 4 again, then step 5. |
| Browser shows **404 Not Found** | Check the address: their username after the `~`, then `/cs450/fun.html`. Usernames are case-sensitive. |
| Page shows but looks broken, or shows code | In Mode B, the paste was cut short or mangled. Redo step 3 with the whole file. In Mode A, read the file back and fix it. |
| Page works on a laptop but not a phone | Ask what happens on the phone, then fix the layout. |

## When you're done, report

- The page address.
- The `curl` number from step 5 (or "not checked" and why).
- Any permission change you made, or "none needed".
- One sentence on what the page does, so the student can compare it with
  their check.

## Sources

- Page address `https://cs.unh.edu/~username/...`: confirmed by the CS 450
  instructor, October 29. The `~/public_html/cs450/` folder: CS 450's
  "Build a public web page with a real AI agent" handout (September 30) and
  the Week 5 build-a-page activity.
- agate login (`ssh your-unh-username@agate.cs.unh.edu`): CS 450's "Get
  OpenCode working" handout (October 21),
  https://blkfin.github.io/cs450/handouts/l14-get-opencode-working.html
- Page rules: the CS 450 build-a-page and study-guide activities.
- Permissions: standard Unix rules for a web server reading files in a home
  folder (`x` on each folder on the path, `r` on the file).
- llms.txt convention: https://llmstxt.org/ (here, the student hands this
  file to the agent directly).
